tagline: The advanced, end-to-end manufacturing partner of choice
hero_kpi_rationale: Quarterly net sales are the longest and most comparable indicator for Flex: thirty-seven quarters taken verbatim from the company's annual and quarterly reports, from $6,008 million in the second calendar quarter of 2017 to $7,928 million in the second calendar quarter of 2026, up 21% year over year, lifted by the Cloud and Power Infrastructure segment which grew from $3,244 million in fiscal 2024 to $6,614 million in fiscal 2026, ahead of the announced spin-off of that business.

kpis.name: Net sales
kpis.explanation: Quarterly net sales of the group, all segments combined.
kpis.description: Thirty-seven quarters of history, from $6.0 billion in Q2 2017 to $7.9 billion in Q2 2026.
kpis.signal: Net sales of $7,928 million in the quarter ended 26 June 2026, up 21% year over year, driven by the Cloud and Power Infrastructure segment.

kpis.name: Annual net sales
kpis.explanation: Net sales for the fiscal year, which ends on 31 March.
kpis.description: Ten years of history. The group returned to growth in fiscal 2026 after two years of decline.

kpis.name: Gross profit
kpis.explanation: Quarterly net sales less cost of sales.
kpis.description: Gross profit is rising faster than sales, reflecting a richer product mix.
kpis.signal: $747 million in the quarter ended 26 June 2026, 9.4% of net sales.

kpis.name: Annual gross profit
kpis.explanation: Gross profit for the fiscal year.

kpis.name: Operating income
kpis.explanation: Quarterly operating income under US accounting standards.
kpis.description: Operating margin of 4.9% on a reported basis, 6.7% on the adjusted basis published by the company.
kpis.signal: $392 million in the quarter ended 26 June 2026.

kpis.name: Annual operating income
kpis.explanation: Operating income for the fiscal year.

kpis.name: Net income
kpis.explanation: Quarterly net income attributable to Flex Ltd, continuing operations.
kpis.description: Restated to exclude Nextracker, spun off in 2023 and 2024, so the series stays comparable over time.
kpis.signal: $285 million in the quarter ended 26 June 2026, diluted earnings per share of $0.76.

kpis.name: Annual net income
kpis.explanation: Net income for the fiscal year, continuing operations.
kpis.description: Ten years of history: $443 million in fiscal 2023, $880 million in fiscal 2026.

kpis.name: Diluted earnings per share
kpis.explanation: Quarterly net income divided by the diluted share count.
kpis.description: Buybacks have shrunk the share count, lifting earnings per share faster than net income.
kpis.signal: $0.76 in the quarter ended 26 June 2026, and a record adjusted $1.00.

kpis.name: Annual diluted earnings per share
kpis.explanation: Diluted earnings per share for the fiscal year.

kpis.name: Capital expenditure
kpis.explanation: Purchases of property, plant and equipment over the fiscal year.
kpis.description: Capital intensity is rising with the data centre build-out.

kpis.name: Quarterly capital expenditure
kpis.explanation: Purchases of property, plant and equipment over the quarter.
kpis.signal: $236 million in the quarter ended 26 June 2026.

kpis.name: Operating cash flow
kpis.explanation: Cash generated by operations over the fiscal year.
kpis.description: Series limited to fiscal 2021 onward: earlier figures in the regulatory data set are inconsistent.

kpis.name: Employees
kpis.explanation: Headcount at the close of the fiscal year, as disclosed in the annual report.
kpis.description: Headcount fell from 200,000 in 2019 to 148,000 in 2024 and 2025, then stabilised.
kpis.signal: 150,000 employees at the close of fiscal 2026, up 1.4%, while sales rose 21% in the following quarter: value added per person is increasing.

kpis.name: Manufacturing sites
kpis.explanation: Number of manufacturing and operating sites disclosed in the annual report.
kpis.description: Around 100 sites in roughly 30 countries, a footprint stable over the period.

kpis.name: Integrated Technology Solutions segment revenue
kpis.explanation: Annual revenue of the segment covering communications, high speed networking, enterprise and premium consumer products.
kpis.description: Largest of the three segments, 40% of group sales.

kpis.name: Regulated Manufacturing Solutions segment revenue
kpis.explanation: Annual revenue of the segment covering industrial, automotive and healthcare manufacturing.
kpis.description: 36% of group sales, the most regulated and least cyclical part of the group.

kpis.name: Cloud and Power Infrastructure segment revenue
kpis.explanation: Annual revenue of the segment covering power, cooling and compute infrastructure for data centres.
kpis.description: Revenue more than doubled in two fiscal years, from $3,244 million to $6,614 million. The company announced on 5 May 2026 its intention to spin this segment off into a separate listed company, targeted for the first quarter of calendar 2027.
kpis.signal: $6,614 million in fiscal 2026, 24% of group sales.

kpis.name: Top 10 customer concentration
kpis.explanation: Share of net sales made with the ten largest customers over the fiscal year.
kpis.description: Concentration is rising with the data centre business: 37% in fiscal 2024, 45% in fiscal 2026. A single customer reached 12% of sales in the quarter ended 26 June 2026, mostly within the Cloud and Power Infrastructure segment.

kpis.name: Share buybacks
kpis.explanation: Amount spent repurchasing ordinary shares over the fiscal year.
kpis.description: No shares were repurchased in the quarter ended 26 June 2026, with $1.1 billion still available under the current plan.

risks.title: Global economic conditions and geopolitical uncertainty
risks.description: A downturn in the global economy or a geopolitical shock would weigh on customer demand, on results and on access to capital markets.
risks.score_rationale: First of the twenty-four risks summarised at the head of the risk factor chapter of the company's fiscal 2026 annual report. Wording states these conditions have already adversely affected the business in the past and could do so again. Trend stable. Macroeconomic category weighted high because it drives the order book of every segment.

risks.title: Spin-off of the Cloud and Power Infrastructure segment
risks.description: The planned separation of the CPI segment into an independent listed company may not be completed on the announced terms or timetable, and carries significant costs and execution risk.
risks.score_rationale: Second of the twenty-four risks summarised at the head of the chapter, therefore very high. Explicit wording: the document states the spin-off may not be completed on the terms or timeline contemplated, if at all. Trend new, the operation was announced on 5 May 2026. Strategic category weighted high because it concerns a quarter of group revenue.

risks.title: Tariffs, trade restrictions and export controls
risks.description: Changes in trade policy, customs duties and export controls disrupt the group's cross-border flows, which span roughly thirty countries.
risks.score_rationale: Third of the twenty-four risks summarised at the head of the chapter. Wording states these measures have already adversely affected results and could do so again, and points to heightened trade volatility. Trend up. Regulatory category weighted high given a manufacturing footprint spread across some thirty countries.

risks.title: Customer concentration
risks.description: A significant share of sales comes from a small number of customers. A decline in sales to any of the largest ones would directly hit results and cash flow.
risks.score_rationale: Fifth of the twenty-four risks summarised at the head of the chapter. Wording quantified in the body: the ten largest customers accounted for 45%, 44% and 37% of net sales in fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024. Trend up. Commercial category weighted high because concentration is measurably increasing.

risks.title: Supply chain disruption and demand forecasting
risks.description: Component shortages, supplier problems and forecasting errors can prevent the company from meeting demand, raise costs or leave excess and obsolete inventory.
risks.score_rationale: Eighth of the twenty-four risks summarised at the head of the chapter. Wording cites past semiconductor supply disruptions, including from export controls, which curtailed production and delayed shipments. Trend stable. Operational category weighted high for a contract manufacturer.

risks.title: IT systems breach and cybersecurity incident
risks.description: A breach of information or physical security systems, or an incident affecting operations, products or third parties, would disrupt the business and expose the company to significant costs and liability.
risks.score_rationale: Fourteenth of the twenty-four risks summarised at the head of the chapter. Wording explicitly cites material disruption, reputational damage and significant costs and liability. Trend stable. Cyber category weighted high by construction.

risks.title: Regulation of data centre development
risks.description: Evolving rules on data centre construction, energy consumption and utility infrastructure could dampen demand for the group's power and cooling products.
risks.score_rationale: Twenty-second of the twenty-four risks summarised at the head of the chapter, therefore low in the order. Conditional wording. Trend new, this factor did not exist in the prior annual report. Regulatory category weighted medium, but tied to the fastest-growing segment.

risks.title: Investment in data centre infrastructure
risks.description: Scaling the Cloud and Power Infrastructure segment requires heavy investment in power, cooling and compute integration capacity. That spending can weigh on margins, and demand for these offerings depends on factors the company does not control, chiefly the pace at which its customers build data centres.
risks.score_rationale: Sixth of the twenty-four risks summarised at the head of the risk factor chapter of the company's fiscal 2026 annual report, therefore among the highest. Direct wording: the document states these investments may adversely affect margins and that demand is subject to factors outside its control. Trend up: segment revenue grew from $3,244 million to $6,614 million in two fiscal years and the group has announced its separation. Financial category weighted high because it bears on the profitability of the group's fastest-growing segment.

ai_positioning.summary: Flex does not build AI models or chips. It manufactures and integrates the physical infrastructure, power, cooling and compute systems, that equips its customers' AI data centres, through its Cloud and Power Infrastructure segment, now being spun off.
evidence: Fiscal 2026 annual report, business section: the company supports the design, manufacture and lifecycle management of power, thermal and compute infrastructure products used for AI data centres and mission-critical applications.
Segment revenue rose from $3,244 million (12% of sales, fiscal 2024) to $4,799 million (19%, fiscal 2025) then $6,614 million (24%, fiscal 2026), a trajectory driven directly by data centre demand.

Earnings release of 29 July 2026: the company states it is helping customers accelerate data centre deployment by solving power, heat and scale challenges through power and cooling technology and scalable IT infrastructure solutions, with quarterly sales up 21%.

Fiscal 2026 annual report, risk factors: a dedicated risk factor now covers risks and uncertainties related to the development and use of artificial intelligence, confirming direct exposure to the AI value chain.
